data.body:
## Legitimacy: DEFECT (not working-as-designed) — cited

Three independent authoritative sources, all violated:

1. **ADR 0026 Decision 1** (`docs/adr/0026-reconciler-three-way-merge-baseline.md:38-42`) defines
   the baseline as a per-pair **"last-synced value"** and asks *"does local still equal what Jira
   had at the last sync?"* (`:22-37`). After rebar pushes `Done`, the last-synced value IS `Done`.
   A baseline still holding `To Do` is therefore not the artifact the ADR specifies — the
   implementation advances it from the last-**fetched** snapshot, which diverges from
   last-**synced** for exactly the fields we pushed in that pass. The guard's premise
   ("local == baseline ⇒ local is unchanged since sync") is false in that window.
2. **`_field_contract.py:70-83`** declares `status` with `conflict_class="state"`, and
   `conflict_resolver.py:29,47-49` defines `resolve_state` as *"Local always wins for state
   fields."* An inbound write that overrides a newer local status inverts that declared class.
3. **`inbound_differ.py:641-645`** states its own invariant: the local-side change
   *"has authoritative priority for the pass."*

Structural precedent: the 39c1 / ed5e omit-vs-clear parent-clear incident is the same shape
(outbound omission -> inbound destructive write) with `parent_id` instead of `status`.

## Test-coverage gap that let it through

ADR 0026's mandated direction-preservation regression cell exists for `title` only (added by
b9b8, `outbound_field_diff.py:47`). `test_inbound_field_sync_directionality.py::test_jira_side_status_change_suppressed`
drives `adapters/jira/outbound_fields._diff_fields`, which has **no production caller** — so
status has never been pinned on the live `diff_canonical_fields` path. Compare `parent`, which
after 88d9 got an explicit `_peer_removed_the_parent` peer-evidence guard
(`outbound_field_diff.py:441-445`); status has no equivalent.

## Two candidate fixes — this needs an operator/design decision, so I am NOT picking one

**Option A — advance the baseline with what we just pushed.** In `_advance_baselines`
(`reconcile.py:514-531`), overlay the successfully-applied outbound mutation values onto
`ctx.curr_snapshot` before calling `set_baseline`, so the baseline means last-*synced* rather
than last-*fetched*. Smallest conceptual change and restores the ADR's own definition.
Open question that makes this non-trivial: a status transition can **soft-fail** (no legal
reverse transition -> `RuntimeError` / `IllegalTransitionError` caught by the backstop at
`applier.py:725-726`, pass still exits 0). Advancing the baseline for a push that did not land
would assert a sync that never happened and mask a genuine divergence. So this must key off
per-mutation success, not off the mutation being emitted.

**Option B — never let inbound win a `state`-class field.** Honour
`_field_contract` / `conflict_resolver` literally: exclude `status` (and possibly the other
`state` fields) from `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` suppression, so outbound always local-wins on
status. Simplest and directly matches the declared conflict class, but it deliberately gives up
mirroring genuine Jira-side status edits, which ADR 0026 Decision 1 chose to support.

Option A preserves both behaviours; Option B trades one away. A also fixes the ABA exposure for
ALL five inbound-mirrored fields (`title`/`description`/`priority`/`status`/`assignee`), which
share the same guard and therefore the same defect — B would only fix the `state` subset.

Whichever is chosen, the RED oracle is the ABA sequence: baseline B, local pushed to A, local
reverted to B before the next pass, assert status is not clobbered; plus a held-firm test that a
genuine Jira-side status edit against an unchanged local status still flows inbound.
